accepted.s: The BGREI programme was launched in 2010-11 primarily for which of the following purposes?
o: Promoting oil-palm cultivation in coastal India
Increasing cotton exports from western India
Replacing rice cultivation with millets in dryland regions
Bringing the Green Revolution to the rice-based cropping system of Eastern India
accepted.x: BGREI, or Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India, was launched in 2010-11 for the rice-based rice-wheat cropping system of Eastern India.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme from its purpose rather than from a similar scheme name.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups of States and region was covered under BGREI?
o: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Ladakh
accepted.x: BGREI covers Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Use the regional cluster to distinguish Eastern India from the established north-western Green Revolution belt.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Food Security Mission (NFSM), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2007-08 for rice, wheat and pulses.
2. Its initial objectives included area expansion, productivity enhancement and improvement of soil fertility.
3. Nutri-cereals were added to it in 2014-15.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NFSM began in 2007-08 for rice, wheat and pulses, with the stated production and soil-fertility objectives. Nutri-cereals were added later, in 2018-19.
accepted.tq: Track the original launch year separately from later additions.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Coarse cereals and commercial crops such as cotton, jute and sugarcane were added to NFSM in:
accepted.x: Coarse cereals and commercial crops, including cotton, jute and sugarcane, were added to NFSM in 2014-15.
accepted.tq: Use the milestone sequence to separate the first expansion from the later nutri-cereal addition.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Nutri-cereals were brought under NFSM from which agricultural year?
accepted.x: Nutri-cereals were added to NFSM in 2018-19.
accepted.tq: Test the exact year of a later programme milestone.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Material (SMSP) was merged into NFSM from:
accepted.x: SMSP was merged into NFSM from 2023-24.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an administrative merger year from the year of renaming.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NFSM was renamed as the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in:
accepted.x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission in 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Match the renamed scheme with its precise milestone year.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the crops covered by NFSNM?
accepted.x: NFSNM covers rice, wheat, pulses, maize, barley, Shree Anna, cotton, jute and sugarcane. Oilseeds and oil palm were moved to the NMEO initiatives.
accepted.tq: Find the crop group transferred to a separate oil mission.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NFSNM:
1. It covers maize and barley.
2. It covers cotton, jute and sugarcane.
3. Oilseeds and oil palm are included in NFSNM rather than in a separate mission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NFSNM covers maize, barley, cotton, jute and sugarcane. Oilseeds and oil palm were moved to NMEO-Edible Oils and NMEO-Oil Palm, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped institutional coverage in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How much was released under NFSNM during 2014-15 to 2024-25?
accepted.x: The amount released under NFSNM during 2014-15 to 2024-25 was Rs 15,166.33 crore.
accepted.tq: Test an exact financial figure with closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NMEO-Oilseeds and NMEO-Oil Palm initiatives aim at approximately what level of production by 2030-31?
accepted.x: The two missions target about 70 million tonnes by 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Link the target figure with the correct mission and terminal year.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's edible-oil import dependence declined from 63.2 per cent in FY16 to approximately what level in FY24?
accepted.x: Edible-oil import dependence fell from 63.2 per cent in FY16 to 56.25 per cent in FY24.
accepted.tq: Test both endpoints of a reported trend without reversing the comparison.
accepted.sec: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bajra, jowar and ragi are major millets. Foxtail, little, kodo and proso are minor millets.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure classification pair and eliminate the reversed groupings.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kodo millet is also called kodon; ragi is finger millet and belongs to the major millet group.
accepted.tq: Use the exact local names to detect the incorrect millet pairing.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: Bajra accounts for approximately what share of India's millet output?
accepted.x: Bajra, or pearl millet, accounts for approximately 60 per cent of India's millet output.
accepted.tq: Test an approximate percentage using a narrow range of plausible alternatives.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: The term 'Shree Anna' is associated with:
accepted.x: Millets have been branded as Shree Anna. The term gained prominence in connection with the International Year of Millets.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a campaign label and the crop category it represents.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: The United Nations declared which year as the International Year of Millets?
accepted.x: 2023 was observed as the UN International Year of Millets, with India actively promoting the initiative.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific year associated with an international agricultural observance.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: Dryland farming in India generally refers to cultivation in areas having:
o: Less than 750 mm rainfall and no assured irrigation
More than 1,500 mm rainfall with assured irrigation
Exactly 1,000 mm rainfall and canal irrigation
Less than 250 mm rainfall with compulsory greenhouse cultivation
accepted.x: Dryland farming is practised in areas receiving less than 750 mm rainfall and lacking assured irrigation.
accepted.tq: Apply both conditions—rainfall limit and absence of assured irrigation—rather than using rainfall alone.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which group of crops is predominantly produced in India's rainfed areas?
accepted.x: Rainfed areas, which constitute about 51 per cent of net sown area, produce most of India's millets, pulses and oilseeds.
accepted.tq: Connect the rainfed-area characteristic with its principal crop group.
accepted.sec: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit  [other exams]

accepted.s: The dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains is:
accepted.x: Rice-wheat is the dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, with paddy followed by wheat as double cropping.
accepted.tq: Identify the standard regional crop sequence rather than an individual crop.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Punjab and Haryana, which combination represents the commonly practised crop rotation?
accepted.x: Punjab and Haryana rotate wheat, paddy, mustard and pulses.
accepted.tq: Use the regional rotation as a complete set, not merely the dominant rice-wheat pair.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Intercropping is best described as:
o: Growing a crop only on fallow land
Sowing the next crop after complete removal of the previous crop
Growing one crop continuously for several years
Growing two or more crops together in definite rows
accepted.x: Intercropping involves growing two or more crops together in definite rows, such as tur with jowar or maize.
accepted.tq: Separate intercropping from mixed cropping by focusing on the definite row arrangement.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following examples represents parallel cropping?
o: Tur and jowar sown together in definite rows
Maize and green gram grown together without competition
The next crop sown into a standing crop before its harvest
Paddy followed by wheat in the same year
accepted.x: Parallel cropping involves two crops of different growth habit and duration growing without competition; maize plus green gram is the stated example.
accepted.tq: Discriminate parallel cropping from intercropping and relay cropping by its no-competition condition.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mixed cropping involves sowing crops together without a definite row pattern.
2. Relay cropping involves sowing the next crop into the standing crop before harvest.
3. Ratoon cropping involves regrowth from stubble, and yield generally falls with each cycle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe mixed cropping, relay cropping and ratoon cropping respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each technical definition to its system before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A pulse-cereal rotation is useful primarily because it:
o: Prevents any crop from being harvested in the year
Removes all nutrients from the soil
Requires continuous flooding of the field
Leaves fixed nitrogen for the succeeding crop
accepted.x: Leguminous pulses fix atmospheric nitrogen and leave fixed nitrogen in the soil for the succeeding cereal crop.
accepted.tq: Apply the biological function of legumes to the purpose of crop rotation.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cropping intensity is calculated by which formula?
o: Gross Irrigated Area / Net Sown Area × 100
Net Sown Area / Gross Cropped Area × 100
Gross Cropped Area / Net Sown Area × 100
accepted.x: Cropping intensity equals Gross Cropped Area divided by Net Sown Area, multiplied by 100.
accepted.tq: Check the numerator and denominator rather than relying on the familiar percentage form.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's cropping intensity was 155.4 per cent in 2021-22. The cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh was reported as approximately 1.88 in 2024-25. Which statement is correct?
o: The Andhra Pradesh figure refers to gross geographical area.
The Indian figure is a ratio and the Andhra Pradesh figure is a percentage.
Both figures represent cropping intensity, but they are expressed in different forms.
Both figures represent net irrigated area.
accepted.x: India's figure is expressed as a percentage, whereas Andhra Pradesh's figure is given as a ratio; both refer to cropping intensity.
accepted.tq: Compare the underlying indicator while accounting for different numerical forms.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the recent diversification of agriculture in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A complete shift from crops to mining
A movement from horticulture towards only wheat cultivation
A movement from food grains towards fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm
A shift from agriculture towards exclusively plantation forestry
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is diversifying from food grains towards fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction of structural change rather than just naming a crop.
accepted.sec: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Planning Commission identified how many agro-climatic zones in the Seventh Plan?
accepted.x: The Planning Commission identified 15 agro-climatic zones during the Seventh Plan.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact number in a standard regionalisation classification.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 15 agro-climatic zones were further divided into:
accepted.x: The 15 agro-climatic zones were subdivided into 72 sub-zones.
accepted.tq: Pair the parent classification with its exact subordinate count.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The agro-climatic zones were delineated mainly on the basis of:
accepted.x: The agro-climatic regionalisation was based on soil, climate and cropping pattern.
accepted.tq: Select the physical-agricultural basis rather than unrelated regional indicators.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Trans-Gangetic Plains — wheat and rice; highest productivity
Upper Gangetic Plains — plantations and jhum
Lower Gangetic Plains — wheat and rice; highest productivity
Eastern Himalayan Region — rice and jute as the principal pair
accepted.x: The Trans-Gangetic Plains include Punjab, Haryana and Delhi and are associated with wheat, rice and the highest productivity. The Upper Gangetic Plains are the core Green Revolution belt, the Lower Gangetic Plains are associated with rice and jute, and the Eastern Himalayan Region with plantations and jhum.
accepted.tq: Use the crop signature of each region to eliminate swapped regional descriptions.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The core Green Revolution belt among the following agro-climatic regions is:
accepted.x: The Upper Gangetic Plains, particularly western Uttar Pradesh, constitute the core Green Revolution belt.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the core belt from the adjoining Trans-Gangetic and Lower Gangetic regions.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Southern Plateau and Hills region?
o: Interior Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: The Southern Plateau and Hills region includes interior Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Locate the southern regional grouping using its state cluster.
accepted.sec: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about India's agricultural area in 2021-22 is correct?
o: Geographical area was 141 million hectares and agricultural land was 77.9 per cent.
Geographical area was 328.7 million hectares and agricultural land was about 54.8 per cent of it.
Geographical area was 77.9 million hectares and agricultural land was 54.9 per cent.
Geographical area was 219.16 million hectares and agricultural land was 42.8 per cent.
accepted.x: India's geographical area was 328.7 million hectares, and about 54.8 per cent was agricultural land in 2021-22.
accepted.tq: Separate the geographical-area figure from net sown, net irrigated and gross cropped area figures.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents India's net sown area and gross cropped area in 2021-22?
o: Net sown area 328.7 MH; gross cropped area 77.9 MH
Net sown area 219.16 MH; gross cropped area 141 MH
Net sown area 141 MH; gross cropped area 219.16 MH
Net sown area 77.9 MH; gross cropped area 120.3 MH
accepted.x: India's net sown area was 141 million hectares and gross cropped area was 219.16 million hectares in 2021-22.
accepted.tq: Distinguish net area from gross area by identifying the larger figure as the repeatedly cropped area.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding irrigation in India in 2021-22:
1. Net irrigated area was 77.9 million hectares.
2. Gross irrigated area was 120.3 million hectares.
3. Gross irrigated area constituted 54.9 per cent of gross cropped area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three figures are correct for 2021-22: net irrigated area 77.9 million hectares, gross irrigated area 120.3 million hectares and gross irrigated area equal to 54.9 per cent of GCA.
accepted.tq: Check each area figure and percentage before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Approximately what percentage of India's net sown area is irrigated?
accepted.x: Only 56.4 per cent of India's net sown area is irrigated.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the percentage of net sown area irrigated from the percentage of gross cropped area irrigated.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Wells and tube wells together provide more than what share of India's irrigation?
accepted.x: Wells and tube wells provide over 63 per cent of India's irrigation.
accepted.tq: Use the source-of-irrigation figure without confusing it with total irrigated-area percentages.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly stated about India's position in world agriculture?
o: India is the largest producer of all food grains.
India is the largest producer of pulses and millets.
India is the largest producer of oil palm and barley.
India is the largest producer of wheat and sugarcane in the world.
accepted.x: India is identified as the largest producer of pulses and millets. The other options make broader claims not supported by the stated facts.
accepted.tq: Reject an overbroad superlative and select the precisely stated crop groups.
accepted.sec: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank  [other exams, GROUP-II]
